paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's people were never meant to run a fan club. The Corinthians were splitting into Team Paul and Team Apollos, and Paul asked, "are you not mere men?" (1 Corinthians 3:4). Paul and Apollos are "servants through whom you believed", and "I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow" (1 Corinthians 3:5-6). I stamp cookies all day and have never grown a single thing, so I get it: God does the growing, and He gets the credit.

So what do we do with our lives? We build, and we build carefully, on the one foundation, "which is Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 3:11). The Day will test each builder's work with fire, and what lasts will be rewarded (1 Corinthians 3:13-14), and even if someone's work burns up, Paul says he "will be saved, but only as if through the flames" (1 Corinthians 3:15). So the question for you, baker, is not which human leader gets your boasting but what you're building on Christ, gold or hay.

And here's the part that should make you stand up straight. You are "God's temple," and "God's Spirit dwells in you" (1 Corinthians 3:16), so stop boasting in men, because "All things are yours" (1 Corinthians 3:21-22). Friend, they were fighting over the window seat and Paul told them they own the plane! Paul ends with "you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God" (1 Corinthians 3:23), and he isn't done with these Corinthians, so keep that oven warm.
